references.text: The continuation of the description of the gold chains on the breastpiece, explaining how the chains are to be attached to braided rings and the gold settings on the ephod.
Describes the execution of what was commanded in chapter 28, including the braided gold chains that were attached to the breastpiece.
Mentions the gold settings (mishbetsot) to which the chains were to be attached; the same Hebrew word is used.
Introduces the gold settings mentioned in verse 14 and provides context for how the chains were to be used.
A parallel text describing the execution of the gold settings with braided edges.
This version confirms that the same type of twisted chains was used on both the ephod and the breastpiece, emphasizing their unity in the priestly garments.
This verse documents the actual fulfillment of the instruction in 28:14, confirming that God's detailed plan was fully carried out.
This verse completes the instruction from 28:14 by describing how the chains are connected to the shoulder pieces, thus forming a complete assembly description.
This verse describes the necessary preparations (the rings) that make it possible to carry out the instruction regarding the chains and their attachment given in 28:14.
This verse is a direct continuation of 28:14 and describes the first step in attaching the twisted chains to the breastpiece.
This verse specifies the location of the lower rings needed to attach the twisted chains described in 28:14.
